preconditions.description: The number of test cases T is between 1 and 10 inclusive.
For each test case, the number of cities N is between 1 and 5000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: len(lines) == T + sum(N_i + 1 for N_i in N_list)
preconditions.description: The input contains exactly T test cases, where each test case starts with N followed by N-1 lines of city pairs.

preconditions.expression: all(len(A) <= 50 and len(B) <= 50 and 1 <= C <= 1000 for A, B, C in all_cards)
preconditions.description: City names have length at most 50, and costs are integers between 1 and 1000.
All city names in the input for a test case are distinct, ensuring a valid path without revisiting cities.

postconditions.expression: len(output_lines) == sum(N_i for N_i in N_list)
postconditions.description: The total number of output lines equals the sum of N for all test cases.

postconditions.expression: all(output_lines[i] == f"{start} {end} {cost}" for i, (start, end, cost) in enumerate(sorted_cards))
postconditions.description: For each test case, the first N-1 lines output the cards in the correct sequential order of the journey.

postconditions.expression: all(int(output_lines[i]) == sum(cost for _, _, cost in sorted_cards) for i in cost_indices)
postconditions.description: The N-th line for each test case contains the sum of costs of all cards in that test case.

postconditions.expression: all(sorted_cards[i][1] == sorted_cards[i+1][0] for i in range(len(sorted_cards)-1))
postconditions.description: The reconstructed sequence of cards forms a valid path where the destination of one card is the origin of the next.

postconditions.expression: len(set(city for city, _, _ in sorted_cards)) == N and len(set(city for _, city, _ in sorted_cards)) == N
postconditions.description: The sequence visits exactly N distinct cities, with no city appearing as a start or end more than once in the path.
